brief.headline: Tech the lone sector holding; everything else under pressure
brief.regime_summary: SPY at 762.63, essentially sitting on its 50DMA (+0.19%) and 1.7% from its 1-year drawdown low. The 1-week return was -0.67% and the 1-month -0.33%, confirming drift, not collapse. VIX at 16.48 is modest but sits above its 20DMA of 15.88, a mild caution flag. Breadth is the real concern: only 2 of 11 sectors have more than half their members above the 50DMA, and only XLK shows positive 20-day momentum (+6.7%). Every other sector is negative on that window, with energy, staples, materials, financials, real estate and utilities all down 4-7%. This is not a broad risk-off tape; it is a concentrated, tech-led holding action in a neutral-to-weakening regime.

portfolio.note: Price 512.90, +2.48% above the 20DMA with RSI 60.4 and positive market RS (+2.0% over 20 days). Earnings Oct 28 are the next event; the position is +25% from cost so no structural reason to act before that date.

Earnings on Oct 14, less than two weeks away. Price 1811.67 sits 6.3% above the 20DMA with trailing P/E of 62.9, 60% above its historical median. All 28 analyst EPS revisions in the last 30 days were upgrades. Hold the position but be aware the gap between price and history multiples leaves little room for a guidance miss.

XLE at 61.50 is 3.1% below the 20DMA, 6.5% from its 20-day high, and the sector has the second-worst 20-day momentum of any sector (-4.5%). The position carries a -30% unrealized loss, and nothing in the near-term energy tape argues for a reversal catalyst.

GLD at 380.84 is 3.8% below its 20DMA and 7.9% off the 20-day high, with RSI 38.7 approaching oversold. Gold spot (GC=F) RSI is 36.7 and 20-day momentum is -4.8%. The thesis that gold holds as a risk hedge is being tested; watch whether RSI holds above 30 or a capitulation flush occurs.

watchlist.name: Micron Technology
watchlist.thesis: MU is the highest-scoring screen name at 1.83. Price 1065.11 is 5.2% above the 20DMA (1012.10) in a full bull MA stack. EPS estimates revised up 134% and revenue estimates up 113% over the past 30 days, following a strong earnings report last week. Forward P/E of 5.3x is undemanding. In the current tape, XLK is the only sector with positive momentum, so this setup has sector tailwind.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: 1012.10, 20-day high: 1108.72, ATR-based stop distance: ~45 points (4.2% of price)
watchlist.risk: Any reversal in DRAM/HBM demand outlook or a broad risk-off shift would hit MU hard given 50% realized volatility.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC at 120.23 has a 35% 20-day momentum, the highest in the screen. It is 10.6% above the 20DMA and 17.9% above the 40DMA. Earnings are Oct 22, so this is an event-driven setup. The 20-day RS vs the market is +34.8%. The mixed DMA stack (100DMA at 108.50 is close to current price) is the one structural caveat.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: 108.75, 20-day high: 127.44, ATR-based stop distance: ~6.2 points (5.1% of price)
watchlist.risk: Vol is 73.6% annualized; a poor earnings print Oct 22 could erase the entire recent move. Estimate revisions are flat, so expectations are not running ahead of consensus.

watchlist.name: Advanced Micro Devices
watchlist.thesis: AMD at 611.76 shows 33.1% 20-day momentum, RSI 66.3, and is 11.3% above the 20DMA in a full bull stack. Market RS is +32.7% over 20 days. Trailing P/E of 156x is high but the growth story (81.7% EPS growth CY) and XLK leadership support the premium. Earnings are Nov 3, so there is runway before the next binary event.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: 549.78 (approx from +11.3%), 20-day high: 638.80 (approx from -4.3%), ATR-based stop distance: ~24 points (3.9% of price)
watchlist.risk: P/E is 55% above historical median; any rotation out of high-multiple growth in a risk-off shift makes AMD particularly vulnerable given its 54.8% annualized vol.

watchlist.name: Meta Platforms
watchlist.thesis: META at 725.18 is 6.2% above its 20DMA with 25.5% 20-day momentum and 18.4% above the 100DMA. Earnings Oct 28 align with MSFT, creating a concentrated tech-earnings week. P/E of 27.9x is only modestly above history (+6.3%). Revenue revisions are essentially flat, so the setup is technical momentum rather than estimate-driven.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: 682.40 (approx from +6.2%), 20-day high: 779.50 (approx from -7.0%), ATR-based stop distance: ~27 points (3.7% of price)
watchlist.risk: EPS revisions have ticked slightly negative (-0.69%) and realized vol is 55.9%; a guidance cut at earnings would break the trend.

watchlist.name: Comcast Corporation
watchlist.thesis: CMCSA at 21.76 is 8.8% below the 20DMA and 20% from the 20-day high, with RSI at 28.3. EPS growth is -19.2% CY and revenue growth is -2.9%. Barclays cut price targets ahead of Q3 earnings Oct 22. The 20-day sector RS is -17.7%. Trailing P/E of 6.97x is slightly above historical median (6.45x), so valuation is not yet a floor.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: 23.85, 20-day high: 27.19, ATR-based stop distance: ~0.67 points (3.1% of price)
watchlist.risk: RSI at 28.3 is technically oversold; a short-squeeze or positive Q3 surprise on Oct 22 could produce a violent cover rally given the weak sentiment positioning.

watchlist.name: Adobe Inc.
watchlist.thesis: ADBE at 239.94 is 4.6% below the 20DMA and 18.1% off the 20-day high. 20-day momentum is -16.1% and sector RS is -22.9%. P/E of 13.0x is 57% below its historical median, suggesting the market has materially de-rated the growth story, not just priced a dip.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA: 251.33 (approx from -4.6%), 20-day high: 293.00 (approx from -18.1%), ATR-based stop distance: ~9.2 points (3.9% of price)
watchlist.risk: Extreme cheapness vs history (P/E at -57% of median) could attract value buyers; next earnings are not until Dec 9 so there is no near-term catalyst to accelerate the move either direction.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Down 2.2% on the week and 4.8% over 20 days, RSI 36.7, sitting 3.5% below the 20DMA with a mixed MA stack. Watch the 30 RSI level as a potential capitulation signal; a failure to hold risks a further move toward 40-day support.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: At 92.17, WTI is 4.0% below its 20DMA but retains a bullish MA stack on the longer-term picture. A 13.7% drop from the 20-day high with RSI at 49 suggests the near-term trend is corrective; watch whether 40DMA support holds.

commodities.name: Brent Crude
commodities.note: Brent dropped 5.7% last week to 100.50 and is 2.3% below the 20DMA; thin liquidity flags in the data amplify headline risk. The 40-day momentum of +26.5% shows the structural bid remains, but the weekly drop warrants watching for confirmation of a base.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: At 6.557, copper is essentially flat vs its 20DMA (-0.46%) with RSI near 49, a neutral read. Extremely elevated relative volume (6.9x average) flags unusual activity worth monitoring as a leading macro indicator.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Down 10.1% on the week to 2.965, the largest commodity drop in the screen. 20-day momentum is near flat (+0.3%) and RSI is 50.8, suggesting the weekly drop was a spike rather than a trend shift, but the high vol (50%) and thin liquidity warrant caution.

risks: Tech earnings concentration: INTC Oct 22, CMCSA Oct 22, ASML Oct 14, MSFT and META Oct 28. A miss from any major name could crack the only sector providing market support.
Breadth deterioration: only 18% of sectors have a majority of members above the 50DMA. Any further weakness turns a neutral regime into a confirmed risk-off tape.
Gold and GLD breaking down despite neutral macro; if the traditional safe-haven is failing to bid, it may signal broader de-risking in real-money portfolios.
Energy sector underperformance: WTI off 13.7% from 20-day high and XLE at -30% unrealized in the portfolio. A further crude drop would compound both the commodity and equity loss.
INTC and AMD elevated vol (73% and 55%) means earnings misses in the Oct/Nov window can produce outsized drawdowns in what have been strong momentum names.
